chunk_findings.detail:
When `value` is present, `_offenders` only flags calls whose `name` is an `ast.Constant` string. A valid test can spell the attribute with a variable:
```python
from ddflow.infra import log as L
def test_x(monkeypatch):
    attr = "APPEND_HOOKS"
    monkeypatch.setattr(L, attr, [])
```
At runtime this rebinds `ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS` while `_eventlog.APPEND_HOOKS` keeps its original binding, so the test passes vacuously. `_offenders` reaches the `isinstance(name, ast.Constant)` check, sees `ast.Name`, and `continue`s, so it reports no offender. This is a direct re-spelling of the exact call this guard claims to catch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_offenders

chunk_findings.detail:
The `value is None` branch misreads `pytest.MonkeyPatch.setattr`. Its signature is `setattr(target, name, value=NOTSET)`, and omitting `value` is documented behavior: it deletes `target.name`. Thus
```python
monkeypatch.setattr(L, "APPEND_HOOKS")
```
is a valid call that removes `ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS` only from the package, while `_eventlog` keeps its own list. `_offenders` puts this call in the `else` branch, then requires `target` to be an `ast.Constant` string; `L` is an `ast.Name`, so it is never reported. The guard can still be bypassed by the deletion form of the same package patch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_offenders

chunk_findings.detail: The scan uses `_TESTS.glob("test_*.py")`, which does not recurse into subdirectories. Pytest recursively collects `tests/**/test_*.py`, so an offending file such as `tests/infra/test_high_water.py` containing `monkeypatch.setattr(L, "APPEND_HOOKS", [])` is never read and the guard test still passes.
